text: Vibha Saraf is an Indian singer-songwriter and Bollywood playback singer who performs and writes music primarily inspired by Kashmiri folk traditions. She has contributed to the soundtracks of the films Raazi, which won Best Film at the 64th Filmfare Awards, and Gully Boy, the fourth highest-grossing Bollywood film of 2019. In 2019, she was jointly nominated with Harshdeep Kaur for Best Female Playback Singer at both the 65th Filmfare Awards and the 20th International Indian Film Academy (IIFA) Awards for the song "Dilbaro" from the 2018 film Raazi. Born in the Fateh Kadal neighbourhood of Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, Saraf's family relocated to New Delhi when she was three years old during the exodus of Kashmiri Pandits. She studied Hindustani classical music for four years at Shriram Bharatiya Kala Kendra before pursuing pop music for five years, and worked as a management consultant for five years before leaving to focus on music. In 2013, she moved to Mumbai to pursue her music career, recording her first soundtrack song, "O Soniye," a duet with Arijit Singh for Titoo MBA in 2014, and later singing "Feeling Avnavi" with Advait Nemlekar for Gujjubhai the Great in 2015. Her debut single, "Harmokh Bartal," was released in 2016, a Kashmiri bhajan reinterpreted with Tapas Relia composing and Ashwin Srinivasan on flute and Ankur Mukherjee on guitar. In 2018, she performed "Dilbaro" for Raazi, a song written by Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy and inspired by the Kashmiri folk wedding song "Khanmoj koor," which earned her a nomination for an IIFA Award in 2019. In February 2019, she released "Kab Se Kab Tak" as a duet with Ranveer Singh, and co-sang "Dil Mein Mars Hai" with Benny Dayal for the Mission Mangal soundtrack, released in summer 2019. That same year, she performed on the Gully Boy soundtrack in the duet "Kab Se Kab Tak" with Ranveer Singh. She has written music for Nucleya, whom she met briefly at an airport, and has composed two songs for him, performing one, "Behka," in the film High Jack. Saraf appears in music videos, including as a co-singer with Rajasthani folk singer Dapu Khan in the "Mumal" video and with Absar Zahoor in her own "Jalwe" video. She has sung in Hindi, Kashmiri, Telugu, Bengali, and Tamil, and writes and composes for both film and independent music. Her music is influenced by traditional music from Kashmir, Jammu, and Ladakh, which she heard from her grandparents and mother, shaping her subconscious connection to Kashmiri music. She expresses a desire to promote the sufism present in her songs and draws inspiration from Kashmiri literature, including the poetry of Habba Khatoon and Lalleshwari. In a 2019 interview with The Hindu, she described her responsibility to share Kashmir-inspired folk music with a broader audience as a duty "falling on our generation" to "stick to our roots," and also expressed appreciation for the preservation and popularity of Punjabi music. Vibha Saraf won the Best Female Playback Singer award for "Dilbaro" from Raazi at the 20th IIFA Awards on 18 September 2019 in Mumbai, India, and also jointly won the Best Female Playback Singer award at the REEL Movie Awards 2019 and the Zee Cine Award for Best Playback Singer – Female for the same song.
